chapter: Postwar Poland and jazz under Stalinism
title: The thaw: Thiermann's concerts and the first Polish jazz stars
summary: A read-aloud text describes jazz returning, concerts organised by Leopold Tiermann, a list of favourite Polish musicians, and the lack of financial support.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. became favorable to Jess. Little sparks sprung up here and there. Mysterious posters appeared on the walls of Warsaw announcing things like performances. Was extremely simple. Just some hole in the railway workers club. Leopold Thiermann, the former Habitue How do you pronounce it? Habitue? Habitue of the IMCA, who later was to become a well-known writer, arranged a series of concerts with the participation of enthusiastic groups from Warsaw, Krakow, Luch. The public throned the halls in crowds never seen before. Their favorites, except of American that can hear from records, became Polish musicians. Matuszkiewicz, sax clarinet, Walasek, sax tenor, Sobocinski drums, Wojciechowski trumpet, Kujawski bass, Guziński trumpet, Trzaskowski and Kurilewicz piano, Byliński drums and Jean Johnston, the rediscovered vocalist of the AMCA days, British wife of the Polish pilot. Unfortunately, the so-called jazz stage had no financial support and very soon the musicians had to separate and were to meet, but from time to time at occasional concerts, chiefly at a yearly meeting at Krakow on All Souls Day that has since become a tradition.
